title: Sun over the horizon
summary: Why watching the solar disk at dawn is the strongest morning-light tier—and how it unlocks the day boost.

sections.heading: What this tier is
sections.body: Sun over the horizon means you are outside as the solar disk clears the horizon, with bare eyes and no window glass between you and the sky. Circadian biology resets from outdoor light intensity and spectrum at the eyes. When the sun itself appears, you get a rapid change in radiance and a solar-path signal indoor LEDs cannot mimic. This is the top sunrise tier in the app.

sections.heading: Why it is the strongest morning signal
sections.body: Glass filters UV and alters spectrum; sunglasses block the dose. Horizon viewing within a tight window around local sunrise is the cleanest natural “day has started” cue. Open-sky and limited-sky outdoor mornings still help—they are lower tiers when weather or terrain block the disk. The hierarchy teaches light quality first, not perfectionism every calendar day.

sections.heading: Practical habit
sections.body: Be outside before the disk clears the horizon when you can. Bare eyes to the sun—no window glass. Bracket local sunrise (shown on Place/Today) within about 15 minutes before or after for full points. Pair with outdoor grounding when practical. Log skin contact and sunglasses on the sunrise check-in because they adjust your day multiplier.

sections.heading: What is solid vs framework
sections.body: Solid ground: morning outdoor light is the strongest non-drug circadian zeitgeber; unobstructed outdoor dawn beats indoor brightness. Framework / teaching layer: exact mitochondrial membrane-alignment claims tied to the disk minute. Dr. Jack Kruse’s light-first teaching ranks horizon sunrise at the top of the morning stack; chronobiology agrees on outdoor morning light without requiring a ritual disk every day.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: Log Sun over the horizon in the sunrise slot when that was your morning signal. It unlocks the highest day boost on other activities. Use open-sky or outside-morning tiers honestly when the disk is not available. Read Why sunrise is the most important part of the day for the full mitochondria and clock lesson. Educational only—not medical advice.
